svg.text: Phase 2 · step 9f · Recalls and bulletins, and compliance: options
Reference documents (#068) from a vehicle's Maintenance › Set up; one-time and recurring requirements; applies, not applicable, under review.
1 · Adding one, in Maintenance › Set up (a Maintainer)
A · Two buttons: a new recall or bulletin, or one already recorded on another vehicle
+ "From one known…" lists the recalls the person can read (on
their other vehicles), to add this vehicle's requirement for one.
− Three buttons in a row (they wrap on phones).
B · One "+ Recall or bulletin": new, or pick one already recorded
+ One button; the choice is inside.
+ The list shows only when there's something to pick.
− One more step for a new one.
2 · The form (either option): the document, then this vehicle's requirement for it
Wide · a dialog (a full-height sheet on phones)
The nut may not be torqued to spec…
Dealers will retorque the nut, free.
One-time: the first finished job that does it closes it.
Not applicable asks why (e.g. "Built after the VIN range").
The PDF (and photos) are added once it's saved, on its
own page, like a document's scans: they're the recall's, so
every vehicle that links it sees them.
The name starts as the title (shortened to 40 characters).
Editing it later changes it for every vehicle that links it,
so only a Maintainer of all of them (or the Admin) may.
3 · The requirement dialog gains the same two choices (any requirement, linked or not)
One-time hides the intervals (an initial deadline is Phase 5).
A linked one shows "Recall · NHTSA 24V-123 · Open it ›" at the top.
Not applicable: a reason field appears under the choice.
4 · The Schedule (everyone): where recalls go, and how each stands
A · One list; closed and ruled-out ones move to the bottom section
Every 5,000 mi or 6 months · last done 12 Oct 2026 at 52,310 mi
One-time · Recall · NHTSA 23V-555 › · Brake job, 2 Mar 2026
B · A section of their own, above your own schedule
Every 5,000 mi or 6 months · last done 12 Oct 2026
Either way: a recall's "›" opens it (its details, PDF, and the vehicles that link it, with Edit for whoever may). A one-time requirement of your own (not a recall)
is in A's list, or in B's "Your schedule". Turned-off ones stay at the very bottom, as today.
5 · Status chips: OPEN (amber) · UNDER REVIEW (grey) · COMPLIED <date> (green) · NOT APPLICABLE (grey, with the reason) · a recurring one shows none
